Forced to flee — localised question form

Version 3 of the item, rendered as it would appear on a form, with the text after each “e.g.” drafted from what was recorded in that country. The response options never change — only the examples, which the question variants document permits localising and which the desk review found respondents depend on.

Read this before using any of it

These are drafts for review, not enumerator text.

The translations are unreviewed. Translating an instrument is a specialist job — TRAPD, or forward-and-back translation with reconciliation — because a question has to be understood the same way, not merely mean the same thing. Cognitive testing on an unreviewed translation tests the translation, not the question. Two words need a professional decision in particular: flee, where several languages separate fleeing-in-panic from leaving-under-duress and the item means the second; and persecution, a legal term of art that in everyday registers reads as ordinary harassment.

The names are UCDP’s, not a respondent’s. UCDP writes “JAS” where a Nigerian respondent says Boko Haram. Actor names are never translated — they are proper nouns.

Identity groups are never named. UCDP codes communal violence as, for example, “Christians (Nigeria) – Muslims (Nigeria)”, and at subnational level as named ethnic groups. Correct as conflict coding, unusable in an instrument a government enumerator reads aloud. Those become “communal or intercommunal violence”.

Naming actors risks anchoring. Someone displaced by a group not named may conclude the option does not cover them. Category phrasing is preferred where the data allows, and every example is tagged with which it is.

Subnational sets appear only where they say something different. A region whose examples merely repeat the national list is not shown.

Sources: UCDP GED for conflict, IDMC for hazards. Generated by prototype-python/build_questions.py. Ctrl/Cmd-P prints the form alone.
